label: All-ring depth three from closed violations
title: Closed violating walks decide the all-ring depth-three set: six nonempty gaps, one window that overstates at ring 16, and depth-two periods that do not survive
kind: Exact all-ring depth-three decision by strong components, with no matrix powers
summary: The eighteenth unit's post hoc identity is a theorem at every depth: a rule has depth at most h on every ring iff its pair graph has no violating three-edge walk closed inside a strong component. Applied to the 65,536-vertex depth-three graph, with no matrix power taken, it gives all-ring depth-three gaps of 8, 10, 10, 6, 8, 4, 0 rules under 232, 4, 32, 200, 22, 90, 150, first failing rings up to 16, and eventual periods 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 6.
takeaway: Depth levels do not inherit each other's arithmetic: the ring window that lies belongs to 200, not to 22 as at depth two, and the period under 22 collapses from 12 to 1 while other observations keep a period on an entirely different set of rules.
